verses.1: If Israel returns, then say, “Yahweh, may You return to me.” But if You remove Your gifts from before me, then do not do so.
verses.2: And may the name of the LORD be blessed truly, in justice and righteousness. May nations rejoice in it, and may they sing to it.
verses.3: For thus said Jehovah to the people of Judah and to Jerusalem: “You shall have peace. Do not sow in the fields.”
verses.4: Lay down your idols before Jehovah, and remove all those idols from your hearts. May the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem do this, so that a fire of wrath may not spread out like a blaze of destruction. No evil thing will be able to harm you because of your enemies.
verses.5: Speak in Judah and in Jerusalem! Let them hear and say, “They will set up a trumpet on the earth.” They will call for a gathering, and they will say, “Let them come together.”
verses.6: Shu-Nes Chiyonah, you should not stand here. For I am in a bad condition; I will bring disaster upon myself.
verses.7: The lion rose from its den. It destroyed nations. It set out from its place to conquer your land. Your cities will be filled with people who have no place to live.
verses.8: So they put on their masks, and they laughed, because Jehovah did not return to them.
verses.9: And on that day, the Lord will destroy the hearts of the king and the rulers. The priests and prophets will also be destroyed.
verses.10: And he said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh! Now you have brought this people and Jerusalem here. May peace be upon you! May the destruction come until it reaches the very bones of your flesh.”
verses.11: On that day, it will be said to the people of this land and to Jerusalem: “A fresh breeze will blow over the sea, through the gates of my people. There will be no more darkness or gloom.”
verses.12: Now, a spirit filled with these qualities comes to me. I will also speak to them about judgments.
verses.13: Look, clouds rise up, and their wings are light, as if they were not attached to anything. Oh, we are in trouble, for our husbands have left us.
verses.14: May the evil of Jerusalem be removed from your heart, so that you may be saved. May your thoughts be free from those evil ones.
verses.15: For the voice of God speaks from heaven, and it makes thunder sound from the heights.
verses.16: Let them remember those nations! Let them hear the cries coming from Jerusalem. They are people who come from distant lands, and they bring their voices to the cities of Judah.
verses.17: When the guards stood around her, I was terrified, oh Lord!
verses.18: Your ways and your actions have brought you this misfortune. It’s sad that your heart has been touched by these things.
verses.19: From afar, from far away… My heart is filled with sorrow. I can’t bear it anymore. For the sound of war has been heard; my soul is in chaos due to the war.
verses.20: “She who destroys everything is called “Shevbar”. She suddenly destroyed the entire land. For a moment, my dwellings were destroyed.”
verses.21: Until the end, I will see miracles and hear voices that are heard.
verses.22: For my people are like wild animals; they do not know anything. They are foolish and ignorant. They are wise in doing evil, but not in doing good. They do not know how to act properly.
verses.23: I saw the earth, and I saw its mountains and rivers. I also saw the heavens, but there was no light in them.
verses.24: I saw the mountains, and there was complete silence. All the valleys were also silent.
verses.25: I saw that there was no man, and all the stars in the sky had disappeared.
verses.26: I saw that the Mediterranean Sea and all its cities were destroyed by Jehovah from before Horon Apos.
verses.27: For as Jehovah said, “Shammeh will be the name of this land.” But I will not do anything to it.
verses.28: Therefore, the earth will mourn, and the heavens will cry out above it. For I have spoken in times past, but they did not listen; I have come back from them, but they will not accept me again.
verses.29: From the heights and from the ruins, all the people of the city rushed away. They fled in all directions. The city was left empty; no one lived there anymore.
verses.30: And you, my husband, do as I command. You must take care of my second child. You must protect him like gold. You must tear his eyes out with your hands. Your soul will be destroyed.
verses.31: For I heard a cry of despair, like the cry of a woman in pain. The girl from Zion cried out loudly, with her face covered in tears. Oh, help me! My soul is exhausted from suffering.
